Definition: Abdi, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Abdi is the name of two Israelites — a Levite, the father of Kish in the singers’ line of Heman, and an ‘Abdi’ among the sons of Elam who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s day. The same name sits in a worship genealogy and in a repentance list.
TheologicalSignificance: Two men, one name: one in the line of temple singers, one in the list of those who put away foreign wives. I believe that is the Bible in miniature — worship and repentance side by side — and both are written down, because God keeps the record of those who serve Him and those who turn back to Him.
